body.heading: The closed-circle habit
paragraphs: Every group has an unspoken seating chart: same people, same jokes, same plans. It feels safe, but it quietly shuts the door on anyone new — the new colleague, the recent arrival, the friend of a friend standing at the edge of the conversation.
Being the person who opens the circle is a small social superpower. An introduction, an invitation, a seat saved — these cost almost nothing and can change someone's whole season.

body.heading: How circles grow well
paragraphs: Start with low-stakes invitations: the group lunch, the walk, the game night with room for one more. New people do not need to be adopted; they need a fair chance to show up twice.
And let old friends grow too. Sometimes making room means accepting that a friend's life now includes people you did not choose. That is not loss; that is what a living friendship looks like.

description: New people can feel like a threat to old routines — but most circles grow better than they break.
